items.stem: In a population of bacteria produced by fission, variation is:
items.markingKey: (a) very little.

items.stem: Which of the following is an acquired trait?
items.markingKey: (a) A tanned skin from sunlight is an acquired trait. The others: blood group – an inherited trait; curly hair – an inherited trait; free or attached earlobes – an inherited trait.

items.stem: Why are traits acquired during a lifetime not inherited?
items.answer: They are changes in body (somatic) cells, not in the DNA of germ cells, so they cannot be passed to offspring.
items.markingKey: 2 marks.

items.stem: Classify these traits as an acquired trait or an inherited trait: (1) ability to swim; (2) blood group; (3) curly hair; (4) knowledge of English; (5) a tanned skin from sunlight.
items.answer: An acquired trait: a tanned skin from sunlight; ability to swim; knowledge of English. An inherited trait: blood group; curly hair.
items.markingKey: ½ mark per correctly placed item (rounded): An acquired trait: a tanned skin from sunlight; ability to swim; knowledge of English. An inherited trait: blood group; curly hair.

items.stem: Which of the following is NOT an inherited trait?
items.markingKey: (c) A tanned skin from sunlight is an acquired trait, not an inherited trait. Each of the others (free or attached earlobes, natural skin colour, colour of the eyes) is an inherited trait.

items.stem: How does the creation of variations in a species promote survival, using the example of a population of red beetles that produces a green variant in green bushes?
items.answer: Crows easily see red beetles on green leaves and eat them; green variants are hidden, survive and reproduce, so the proportion of green beetles increases.
items.markingKey: 1 mark variation. 1 mark selection. 1 mark survival.

items.stem: Mendel used which plant for his experiments?
items.markingKey: (c) garden pea.

items.stem: In a monohybrid cross between pure tall and pure dwarf pea plants, 1000 F2 plants are produced. How many are expected to be pure tall (TT)?
Why did Mendel choose pea plants for his experiments?
items.answer: They have many clear contrasting traits, a short life cycle, produce many seeds, and can be easily self- and cross-pollinated.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each (any two).

items.stem: A yellow pea plant of unknown genotype is crossed with a green plant (yy) and gives all 100 yellow plants. What is the genotype of the yellow plant? Explain.
items.markingKey: No recessive offspring means the plant gave only Y gametes: homozygous dominant.

items.stem: A pure violet pea plant (VV) is crossed with a pure white plant (vv) for flower colour. The F1 plants are self-pollinated and 400 F2 plants are obtained. How many F2 plants are expected to be white? What is the F2 genotypic ratio?
items.markingKey: F1 all Vv (violet). F2 phenotypes 3 violet : 1 white, so white = 400/4 = 100. Genotypes 1 : 2 : 1.

items.stem: Pure yellow tall pea plants are crossed with pure green dwarf plants. If 160 F2 plants are obtained, how many of each phenotype are expected?
items.answer: yellow tall: 90; yellow dwarf: 30; green tall: 30; green dwarf: 10

items.stem: In a monohybrid cross between pure green and pure yellow pea plants, 400 F2 plants are produced. How many are expected to be green (showing the dominant trait)?
Describe Mendel's dihybrid cross between round yellow and wrinkled green seeded pea plants. What is the F2 ratio, and what does it show?
items.answer: P: RRYY × rryy; F1: RrYy (round yellow). F1 selfed gives 16 combinations: 9 round yellow : 3 round green : 3 wrinkled yellow : 1 wrinkled green. It shows that the two traits are inherited independently (new combinations appear).
items.markingKey: 2 marks cross; 2 marks ratio; 1 mark conclusion.

items.stem:
Read: Mendel crossed pure tall (TT) pea plants with pure dwarf (tt) plants. All F1 plants were tall. He then self-pollinated the F1 plants and got 1064 F2 plants: 787 tall and 277 dwarf.
(i) Which trait is dominant? (ii) What is the genotype of F1 plants? (iii) Calculate the approximate ratio of tall to dwarf in F2. (iv) What will be the genotypes of the tall F2 plants?
items.answer: (i) Tall. (ii) Tt. (iii) 787 : 277 ≈ 2.84 : 1, about 3 : 1. (iv) TT and Tt (in the ratio 1 : 2).
items.markingKey: 1 mark each part.

items.stem: A pure round pea plant (RR) is crossed with a pure wrinkled plant (rr) for seed shape. The F1 plants are self-pollinated and 1000 F2 plants are obtained. How many F2 plants are expected to be wrinkled? What is the F2 genotypic ratio?
items.markingKey: F1 all Rr (round). F2 phenotypes 3 round : 1 wrinkled, so wrinkled = 1000/4 = 250. Genotypes 1 : 2 : 1.

items.markingKey: No recessive offspring means the plant gave only V gametes: homozygous dominant.

items.stem: In a monohybrid cross between pure yellow and pure green pea plants, 1000 F2 plants are produced. How many are expected to be yellow (showing the dominant trait)?

A cross between a tall plant with round seeds and a dwarf plant with wrinkled seeds gives all tall, round plants in F1. What can you conclude? What proportion of F2 plants would be dwarf with wrinkled seeds?
items.answer: Tall and round are dominant. F2 gives 9 : 3 : 3 : 1, so 1/16 are dwarf wrinkled.
items.markingKey: 1 mark dominance. 1 mark ratio. 1 mark 1/16.

items.stem: If the enzyme that makes a plant hormone works efficiently, the plant will be:
items.markingKey: (c) tall.

items.stem: How do genes control the characteristics of an organism? Explain using plant height.
items.answer: A gene codes for a protein (enzyme); in pea plants the enzyme makes a growth hormone; an efficient enzyme gives more hormone and a tall plant, while a less efficient one gives a dwarf plant.
items.markingKey: 1 mark gene → protein. 1 mark hormone → height.

items.stem: Body cells of rice contain 24 chromosomes. How many chromosomes are present in their gametes and in the zygote? Explain.
items.markingKey: Gametes have one set (12); fertilisation of two gametes restores 24 in the zygote.

items.stem: Body cells of humans contain 46 chromosomes. How many chromosomes are present in their gametes and in the zygote? Explain.
items.markingKey: Gametes have one set (23); fertilisation of two gametes restores 46 in the zygote.

items.stem: A man with blood group A marries a woman with blood group O, and their daughter has blood group O. Is this enough to tell whether the A or the O trait is dominant? Why or why not?
items.answer: No. The daughter could get O from both parents if the father is heterozygous (AO); with one family we cannot test dominance — more data are needed (actually A is dominant over O).
items.markingKey: 1 mark no. 1 mark heterozygous father. 1 mark more data.

items.stem: Nikhil's parents already have 1 daughter. What is the probability that their next child will be a son? Explain using the sex chromosomes.
items.markingKey: Mother gives X; father gives X or Y with equal chance; each birth is independent of earlier ones, so P(son, XY) = 1/2.

items.stem:
Read: In a hospital in Lucknow, a woman is blamed by her in-laws for giving birth to three daughters in a row.
(i) What are the sex chromosomes in a woman and a man? (ii) Who decides the sex of the child? (iii) What is the probability of a son in the fourth birth? (iv) Show the inheritance with a simple cross.
items.answer: (i) Woman XX; man XY. (ii) The father. (iii) 50%. (iv) XX × XY → XX, XY, XX, XY: half girls, half boys.

items.stem: Why is the probability of a boy or a girl about 50% in each birth?
items.answer: Half the sperms carry X and half carry Y, and each has an equal chance of fertilising the egg.
